lines.japanese: 満員電車の人ごみに押されながら、前日のアルバイト体験を思いだしていた。
lines.english: Pressed in by the crowd on the packed train, I thought back on the previous day's work experience.

lines.japanese: 想像していたよりもハードな肉体労働で身体は疲れてしまったけれど、気分的にはとても充足していた。
lines.english: The physical labor had been harder than I imagined and left my body tired, but inwardly I felt deeply fulfilled.

lines.japanese: 社会経験のそう多くない僕にとって、一日とはいえ気心の知れた仲間と働けたことは、楽しみながら学べるまたとない機会だった。藤野君には感謝したい。
lines.english: I had little experience of the working world, so even a single day spent working beside friends I knew well had been a rare chance to learn while enjoying myself. I wanted to thank Fujino.

lines.japanese: 「くすくす、ふふふ……」
lines.english: “Hehe, hehehe...”

lines.japanese: うん？
lines.english: Hm?

lines.japanese: ふと忍び笑いが漏れきこえてきたので声の源を辿れば、いつものあの子だった。
lines.english: A stifled laugh suddenly reached me. When I traced it to its source, I found the usual girl.

lines.japanese: 「うふ、うふふ……へへ、えへへ、うひひ……」
lines.english: “Hee-hee... Eheh... Heh-heh... Eeh-heh-heh...”

lines.japanese: 目蓋を下ろして幸せそうに揺れている。長い髪に隠れて見えないけれど、イヤホンでお笑い芸人のラジオでも聞いているのかもしれない。
lines.english: Her eyes were closed, and she swayed happily. Her long hair hid them from view, but perhaps she had earbuds in and was listening to a comedian's radio show.

lines.japanese: 見ているだけで伝染りそうな笑顔。こんな風に笑える子は、周囲のひとびとさえ楽しい気分にさせられるのだろう。
lines.english: Her smile felt contagious even from a distance. A girl who could laugh that way must make the people around her cheerful too.

lines.japanese: きのう名前を教えてもらったのだけど、たしか……しだ、しだ……そうだ、鴨志田さんだ。
lines.english: She had told me her name yesterday. It was... shida, shida... Right. Kamoshida.

lines.japanese: 「どゅわああああー！」
lines.english: “Dwaaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「ひぶっ！？」
lines.english: “Hbib?!”

lines.japanese: 不意の急制動に、車体が大きく揺れた。
lines.english: A sudden hard brake sent the whole car rocking.

lines.japanese: 「あたた……」
lines.english: “Ow ow...”

lines.japanese: そのせいで、鴨志田さんは手すりに額をぶつけたようだ。空いている手で患部を撫でさする仕草が、幼い子供みたいで可愛らしい。
lines.english: Kamoshida seemed to have struck her forehead against the handrail. The way she rubbed the sore spot with her free hand was charmingly childlike.

lines.japanese: 「あら、たんこぶ。ごめんなさいね。でもアナタ、目を閉じたまま嬉しそうにクネクネ揺れてるから……」
lines.english: “Oh, you’ve got a bump. I’m sorry. But you were wriggling around so happily with your eyes shut...”

lines.japanese: 「あっはい、気にしないでください、私がぽけぽけしてたのが悪いんです」
lines.english: “Oh, yes, please don't worry. It's my fault for spacing out.”

lines.japanese: ぶつかってきた女性客に、おでこを隠しながらにっこり微笑んでいる。
lines.english: She hid her forehead and smiled at the woman who had bumped into her.

lines.japanese: ちょっと小鳩に似ているかもしれない。眺めていると、ほのぼのできそう──
lines.english: Maybe she resembled Kobato a little. I felt as though I could relax just by watching her—

lines.japanese: 「あばあっ！？」
lines.english: “Abaah?!”

lines.japanese: ──ああ、またぶつけてる。
lines.english: —oh. She hit it again.

lines.japanese: 失礼ながらちょっと笑ってしまった。
lines.english: It was rude of me, but I laughed a little.
“Owww... Ow... Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫？」
lines.english: “Are you all right?”

lines.japanese: 不意に目が合ったので、思わず声をかけてしまった。なんだか妹みたいな女の子で放っておけない。
lines.english: Our eyes met unexpectedly, and I called out without thinking. Something about her made her seem like a little sister I couldn't leave alone.

lines.japanese: 鴨志田さんはぽっかり口を開けたまま、慌てて何度も頷いた。
lines.english: Kamoshida's mouth fell open, then she hurriedly nodded again and again.

lines.japanese: いきなり話しかけて驚かせてしまったのかもしれない。ますます小鳩みたいで、ちょっと愉快。
lines.english: Perhaps I had startled her by speaking out of nowhere. She seemed more like Kobato by the second, which amused me.

lines.japanese: 「そう、良かった」
lines.english: “Good. I'm glad.”

lines.japanese: つい僕は「優しい兄貴」を気取った口調になってしまう。
lines.english: Without meaning to, I adopted the tone of a kind older brother.

lines.japanese: 「あはは、なんだか昨日と同じようなこと言ってるね」
lines.english: “Ahaha. This is starting to sound like yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes.”

lines.japanese: 笑う僕に対し、彼女の表情は警戒するように硬くなった。まるで初対面の馴れ馴れしい上級生を相手に、困惑しているみたいだ。
lines.english: As I laughed, her expression stiffened warily. She looked confused, like a girl dealing with an overly familiar upperclassman she had only just met.

lines.japanese: 僕は表情と声色に、努めて誠実さを注して言った。
lines.english: I made a deliberate effort to put sincerity into my face and voice.

lines.japanese: 「あれ、覚えてないかな、昨日もここで会ってるんだけど」
lines.english: “Don't you remember? We met here yesterday too.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: よかった、忘れられてるわけではないらしい。
lines.english: Good. Apparently she hadn't forgotten me.

lines.japanese: でも緊張したようなぎこちなさは抜けてない。小鳩と同じで人見知りする子なのか、それとも単に、僕とは親しくしたくないだけなのか。
lines.english: But she still looked tense and awkward. Was she shy around strangers like Kobato, or did she simply have no desire to become friendly with me?

lines.japanese: 友達が増えるのは嬉しいことだけれど、森里君や渡来さんに教えてもらったとおり、僕は相手の顔色というものを窺うことにした。
lines.english: Making more friends would make me happy, but Morisato and Watarai had taught me that I needed to pay attention to the other person's reaction.

lines.japanese: 彼女にもう少しだけ話しかけてみて、それでも僕との対話に乗り気が見られなければ、それ以上踏みこまないようにしよう。
lines.english: I would speak to her just a little more. If she still showed no desire to engage with me, I wouldn't press any further.

lines.japanese: 「鴨志田さん、たしか結構前から、この時間のこの車両だよね」
lines.english: “Kamoshida, you've been riding in this car at this time for quite a while, haven't you?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: まずは分かりきっていることから訊いてみたが、いきなり彼女はきょとんとしてしまった。
lines.english: I started by asking about something obvious, but she immediately stared at me in confusion.

lines.japanese: 「あれ、違う？」
lines.english: “Am I wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、そう、です、けど……」
lines.english: “Oh, no. That's... right, but...”

lines.japanese: もごもごと口ごもるように答えながら、ついには黙りこんでしまう。
lines.english: She mumbled the words and finally fell silent.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの？　鴨志田さん？」
lines.english: “Is something wrong, Kamoshida?”

lines.japanese: やはり僕とは話したくないのだろうか。仕方ない、誰にだって相手を選ぶ権利はある。世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: Perhaps she didn't want to talk to me after all. That couldn't be helped. Everyone had the right to choose their company. May peace prevail on Earth.

lines.japanese: だから、次で最後。最後にもう一度だけ、言葉の握手を求めてみよう。
lines.english: So the next attempt would be my last. I would extend a verbal handshake just once more.

lines.japanese: これで彼女に僕の手を取る意思が見られなければ、諦めて今後はもう声をかけないようにしよう。
lines.english: If she showed no desire to take my hand, I would give up and never speak to her again.

lines.japanese: そして話下手な僕なりに、せいいっぱい頭を回転させて、冗談をひとつ言ってみることにした。
lines.english: I turned my mind as hard as my poor conversational skills allowed and decided to try a joke.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、私、はや──」
lines.english: “Um, I... Haya—”

lines.japanese: 「鴨志田さんっていい名前だよね。おれも下の名前に鷹っていう字が入ってるから、鷹と鴨で鳥繋がりだね。あはは」
lines.english: “Kamoshida is a nice name. Your name has a duck in it, and mine has a hawk—guess that makes us birds of a feather. Ahaha.”
“Y-yes...”

lines.japanese: まったく受けなかった。
lines.english: It didn't land at all.

lines.japanese: 自分のユーモアセンスの無さについて、激しく呪いたくなったその瞬間──
lines.english: At the very instant I began violently cursing my own lack of a sense of humor—

lines.japanese: 「どぅえええええ！」
lines.english: “Dweeeeeeeh!”

lines.japanese: 「ひゃあああ……」
lines.english: “Aaaaaah...”

lines.japanese: ──幸い、ふたたび訪れた群衆の津波が僕と鴨志田さんとを引きはなして、白けた空気をうやむやに洗いながしてくれた。
lines.english: —fortunately, another tidal wave of bodies tore Kamoshida and me apart, washing away the awkward silence in its wake.

lines.japanese: そうして僕らは終着駅へ辿りつくまで言葉を交わさなかった。
lines.english: After that, we exchanged no more words before reaching the terminal station.
“Sigh...”

lines.japanese: 「あたっ！」
lines.english: “Ow!”

lines.japanese: 向こうで鴨志田さんはまた頭をぶつけていた。
lines.english: Across the car, Kamoshida had hit her head again.

lines.japanese: ところで駅へ降りたあと、今度は彼女の方から呼びとめられたのだけれど、それはまたの機会に話そう。
lines.english: As it happened, she was the one who stopped me after we got off at the station—but that is a story for another time.
